title: XGBoost model predicts elevated depressive symptoms in COPD across three cohorts
summary: Seven machine learning algorithms were compared on 1,899 COPD patients from HRS and 2,206 from CHARLS; XGBoost performed best (training AUC 0.824, internal validation AUC 0.757). External testing in 538 patients from ELSA gave an AUC of 0.785 (95% CI 0.748-0.824). It is a cross-sectional design with harmonized depression cutoffs and modest discrimination, and SHAP is not causal.
ai_technology: XGBoost and six other algorithms after recursive feature elimination, with SHAP interpretation

evidence.tested: External test in the ELSA cohort (n=538), cross-sectional data.
evidence.unknown: Prospective prediction, clinical utility and effect of the harmonized cutoffs; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts concurrent elevated depressive symptoms from eight variables.
